newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech opposition overtakes government party - poll.
newsitem.headline: Czech opposition overtakes government party - poll.

text.p: The leading Czech opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD) has overtaken Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's ODS party in an opinion poll just five weeks before nationwide Senate elections, results released on Monday showed.

The poll, conducted last month by the private Factum agency, found that 24.4 percent of the 2,073 potential voters surveyed would support Senate candidates from the centre-left CSSD, while 23.7 percent would vote for Klaus's centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS).
It is the first time since pre-Senate election polls began in July that the CSSD has led the ODS, Factum said.

Elections for the Senate, the upper house of the Czech parliament, will be held for the first time in the country's history on November 15 and 16, under a first past-the-post system in 81 constituencies.
The Senate will have limited powers, such as those of amendement, which can be subsequently overturned in the lower house with a sufficient majority.

The November vote will be the first test of the newly aligned Czech political landscape after elections to the lower house deprived Klaus's coalition of its majority and made the CSSD the second biggest party.

The survey also showed that the Social Democrats would erase ODS' 3.3 percent August lead in preferences for the lower house of parliament, the Chamber of Deputies, if elections were held immediately, a trend other recent polls have also shown.
But the poll suggests that the ruling coalition, including ODS, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) and the Christian- Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), would take a majority in the 200-seat lower house.
In June, the coalition lost its majority in a general election, winning only 99 seats under the proportional representation system used for the lower house.
The poll also showed the far-right Republican Party (SPR-RSC) would not exceed the five percent threshold necessary for winning seats in the chamber. It managed eight percent in the last election.
PREFERENCES (PCT) SEPTEMBER AUGUST JUNE ELECTION RESULT
